_comment: Paraphrase/variant expressions of each canonical proposition in propositions.json. Policy (v0.2, per round-2 review): a prose variant is EQUAL to its proposition_id only if it doesn't silently drop a restriction for which a REAL, named counterexample exists in the domain (e.g. Invar-type low-expansion alloys for K004m, water's 0-4C density anomaly for K015, altitude for boiling point, non-uniform motion for instantaneous speed). Where such a counterexample exists, the unqualified/generic-sounding phrasing is marked 'deliberate_error':'context_dropped' instead of silently left as a false EQUAL. Bare equation-form variants (no natural-language totalizing claim) are treated as carrying the same implicit textbook-standard assumptions as their canonical statement.

variants.text: Voltage across a resistor is the product of current and resistance.
For an ohmic conductor, V/I is constant and equal to R.
V = IR
def voltage(current, resistance): return current * resistance
For an ordinary metal, away from any phase transition, heating it increases its electrical resistance.
Metal resistors get more resistive as they warm up.
variants.notes: Drops the PTC-regime / no-phase-transition / no-superconducting-transition exclusions. Correct relation to K002: ENTAILED_BY (as an unqualified universal claim it would entail K002's restricted case; K002 doesn't license the unqualified generalization).

variants.text: dR/dT > 0 for an ordinary metal in its normal (non-transitional) operating range
As temperature rises, a metal's resistance rises with it.
variants.notes: Same omission as V002b -- kept as a second decoy since this phrasing (bare 'a metal') is an extremely common way the law gets overstated.

variants.text: Semiconductor resistance falls as temperature rises.
variants.notes: Drops the intrinsic/fixed-doping qualifier -- sign and magnitude depend on semiconductor type and doping level.

variants.text: dR/dT < 0 for an intrinsic semiconductor such as silicon, at fixed doping
Heating an intrinsic semiconductor like silicon makes it a better conductor (lower resistance).
For an ordinary solid, increasing its temperature at fixed pressure makes it get longer.
Thermal expansion causes solids to increase in size as temperature rises.
variants.notes: Drops the 'ordinary / positive-expansion-regime' qualifier -- negative-thermal-expansion solids exist (e.g. some zirconium tungstates).

variants.text: dL/dT > 0 for an ordinary solid in its positive-expansion regime, at constant P
Metals expand when heated.
variants.notes: Drops the 'ordinary metal' qualifier -- special low-expansion alloys (e.g. Invar, an Fe-Ni alloy prized for near-zero thermal expansion) are real named counterexamples.

variants.text: For an ordinary metal, not a special low-expansion alloy, heating it causes it to get bigger.
dL/dT > 0 for an ordinary metal, excluding special low-expansion alloys like Invar
Copper expands when heated.
variants.notes: EQUAL under the default reading (solid copper, below melting point, no phase transition) -- copper has no Invar-style exception, unlike K004m's generic 'metal' case. Do NOT merge with K004m or K004 despite the near-identical phrasing -- specialization, not equality (see P02/P03).

variants.text: A copper rod gets longer as its temperature increases.
Density is mass per unit volume.
rho = m/V
Divide an object's mass by its volume to get its density.
For an ideal gas, pressure times volume equals the amount of gas times the gas constant times temperature.
PV = nRT
Ideal gases obey PV=nRT.
For an object of constant mass at everyday (non-relativistic) speeds, force equals mass times acceleration.
F = ma
The net force on an object of constant mass is proportional to its acceleration, with mass as the constant of proportionality.
A liquid starts boiling once it reaches the boiling point for the current pressure.
Boiling occurs exactly when a liquid's temperature meets or exceeds its pressure-dependent boiling point.
Water boils at 100 degrees C at sea-level atmospheric pressure.
At 1 atm, water's boiling point is 100C.
Water boils at 100 degrees C.
variants.notes: Decoy: omits the 1-atm condition. At altitude water boils below 100C. See P06: K009 is ENTAILED_BY V009c (read as an unqualified universal claim), not EQUAL to it.

variants.text: Electrical power is current times voltage.
P = IV
Power dissipated in a resistor is current squared times resistance.
P = I^2 R
v = d/t, for an object moving at constant speed
Instantaneous speed always equals distance divided by time.
variants.notes: Decoy: drops the constant-speed qualifier. For non-uniform motion, instantaneous speed is a derivative, not distance/time. See P07: K012 is ENTAILED_BY V012c (read as an unqualified universal claim), not EQUAL to it.

variants.text: For an object that doesn't change phase while being heated, the heat added equals its mass times specific heat times the temperature change.
Q = mcDeltaT
A smaller radius gives a higher escape velocity, for the same mass.
As a collapsing core's radius shrinks at fixed mass, its escape velocity rises.
Water expands when heated.
variants.notes: Decoy (fixed in v0.2 -- was wrongly left as a plain 'equal' variant in v0.1). True only above 4C; between 0C and 4C water contracts as it warms (K016). Correct relation to K015: ENTAILED_BY-style if read as an unqualified universal claim, but really should just be recognized as UNDER-SPECIFIED rather than paraphrastic.

variants.text: Liquid water's volume increases with temperature, above 4 degrees C.
For a fixed mass of liquid water, volume increases as it is heated from 4C up toward its boiling point.
Between 0C and 4C, water contracts as it warms.
Water reaches its maximum density at 4C, having contracted while heating from 0C to 4C.
Current is the rate at which charge flows.
I = dQ/dt
All metals are conductors.
Being a metal implies being a conductor.
Nothing is both a metal and a semiconductor.
Metal and semiconductor are mutually exclusive material classes.
Doubling every linear dimension of an object multiplies its volume by eight.
def scale3d_volume(volume, k): return volume * k**3
